AGENDA
  ARTS & CULTURE COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Welcome to the Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVD’s of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing
anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp. PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request.
Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting,
and are public records, will be available for review in the office of the Director of the Library, Arts and Culture Department, 222 E. Harvard Street, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA
91205. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the office of the Director of the Library, Arts and Culture
Department, at (818) 548-2030 during regular business hours.

  Thursday, January 17, 2019 at 2:00pm

  1. ROLL CALL
  Report of Recorder Regarding Posting of Agenda.
  The Agenda for the January 17, 2019 meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City
  Hall on January 14, 2019.

  2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  A. Approval of Meeting Minutes from December 20, 2018, at 2:00 p.m.

  3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  A. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Chuck Wike, Community Relations Manager.

  4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items not on this agenda. Each speaker is allowed 5 minutes.
  Commission may question or respond to the speaker but there will be no debate or decision.
  The Commission may refer the matter to City staff for investigation and report.

  5. BUSINESS AGENDA
  A. Action Item(s)
  1. Selection of a Chairperson to serve a one-year term, beginning January 2019.
  2. Selection of a Vice-Chairperson to serve a one-year term, beginning January 2019.

  6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

  7. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

  8. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is February 21, 2019, at 2:00 p.m.
  in the City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, January 17, 2019 at 2:00 p.m.
1. ROLL CALL
   The meeting was called to order on January 17, 2019 at 2:09 p.m.
   Present: Commissioners Oshagan, Zadorian, Vice Chair Vidor, Chairperson Sahakian
   Absent: Commissioner Der Hovanessian
   The Agenda for the January 17th Regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall on
  January 14, 2019.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  A. Approval of Regular Meeting Minutes, as amended, from December 20, 2018
  Moved:  Vice Chair Vidor
  Seconded:  Commissioner Zadorian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Zadorian, Vice Chair Vidor, Chairperson Sahakian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Der Hovanessian
  Abstain:  Commissioner Oshagan

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  A. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Chuck Wike, Community Relations Manager
   Mr. Wike gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts & Culture locations.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker(s):
  1. None

5. BUSINESS AGENDA
  A. Action Item Item(s)
  1. Selection of a Chairperson to serve a one-year term, beginning January 2019
   Chair Sahakian opened the floor to nominations.
   Commissioner Zadorian nominated Vice Chair Vidor. There were no other nominations. Vice Chair Vidor
  accepted nomination.

  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Zadorian, Vice Chair Vidor, Chairperson Sahakian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Der Hovanessian
  Abstain:  None

  1
  2. Selection of a Vice Chairperson to serve a one-year term, beginning January 2019
   Chair Vidor opened the floor to nominations.
   Commissioner Oshagan nominated Commissioner Zadorian. There were no other nominations.
  Commissioner Zadorian accepted the nomination.

  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Sahakian, Vice Chair Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Der Hovanessian
  Abstain:  None

6.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
   Mr. Wike stated that, over the next month and a half, 13-18 year old teens, grades 9th -12th will have an
  opportunity to submit an application for a teen library card design competition that will be used at all library
  locations.
    Commissioner Oshagan asked whether there was an update on the 2019-2019 Work Plan and RFP for a
  Consultant. Dr. Shaffer stated that:
   As discussed at the last meeting, the City Council approved the Work Plan two days before the
  December Commission meeting;
   He has had meetings with other departments on that specific question of staffing and there is one
  more meeting scheduled later in the month;
   He hopes to have a better update at the next meeting; and
   Hiring of staff or a consultant is moving forward as quickly as possible, as it is a City process.
    Vice Chair Zadorian thanked Commissioner Oshagan for nominating her as Vice Chair and she is looking
  forward to working with fellow Commissioners.
    Commissioner Sahakian thanked his colleagues and staff. He stated that it was an honor to serve as
  Chairperson for the past year and the Commission has accomplished a great deal as a team.
    Chair Vidor:
   Stated that she strongly agrees with Commissioner Oshagan’s concern about the hiring of a
  consultant and requested a standing staff update on the hiring’s progress. Dr. Shaffer re-stated
  that staff is moving as quickly as possible;
   Suggested some form of recognition process for artists and asked how the Commission can move
  forward with the process and requested that it be placed on the agenda for February’s
  Commission meeting; Vice Chair Zadorian supports recognizing individual artists, groups or
  organizations; and
   Introduced the idea of the Commission’s co-sponsoring a presentation by the Robby Poblete
  Foundation, about the Art of Peace gun buyback program that transforms weapons into art pieces.
  Dr. Shaffer stated it could be placed as an agenda item for the next meeting.
    Dr. Shaffer stated that:
   The Library Arts & Culture department in conjunction with the City’s Community Development
  Department, as well as Glendale Arts and other art organizations, submitted a grant application to
  the California Arts Commission requesting grant dollars to support programmatic activation in the
  Arts & Entertainment district on Artsakh Avenue; and
   He will keep the Commission advised if the grant is approved.

    Chair Vidor reopened Commission/Staff comments so that Commissioner Oshagan may speak; he asked
  if there was a current art plan for the Adams Square Mini Park Gas station. Dr. Shaffer stated there would
  be a report next month to discuss different options for this location.
  2
 7. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
   Email Communication from Cathy Hrenda supporting Commission activities at Adams Square Mini Park
  Gas Station.
   Email Communication from Jennifer Bentson of Forest Lawn Museum regarding “Women of Vision” Art
  Exhibition in Glendale.

8. ADJOURNMENT – 2:47 p.m.

The next regular meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is February 21, 2019, at 2:00 p.m. in the City Council
Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor.
